clue.text: Hospital supported by boss of our paper given recognition

parts.note: H is the standard abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs
something supported by another sits on it, so the phrase gives ON
the boss of our paper is our editor, OUR plus ED, the usual abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: A hospital, backed by our newspaper's editor, receives some official recognition.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue H sits on top of OUR ED, which is how 'supported by' places it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone honoured has been given public recognition, such as an award or title.

clue.text: Card player to scoff, taking in his opponent

indicators.note: to take in is to contain, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to scoff food is to eat it greedily
at bridge South sits as an opponent of ..., and S is the abbreviation

explanation.surface: A card player eats greedily while drawing in his rival.
explanation.walkthrough: At bridge the four seats are named for compass points; North and South play against East and West.
explanation.definitionFit: East is one of the four seats at a bridge table, so names a card player.

parts.note: an age is a period of history

explanation.surface: Fashion trends drawn from a period on the political right.
explanation.definitionFit: A rage is a craze, the fashion of the moment, as in 'all the rage'.

indicators.note: making signals that the letters of the words are used to build something new

explanation.surface: The hot weather is making the air force crews work hard.
explanation.definitionFit: In athletics a heat is a qualifying race, an eliminating round of a competition.

parts.note: a ham is an actor who overacts badly

explanation.surface: A second-rate overacting performer plays a part in a party game of charades.
explanation.definitionFit: A charade can mean an absurd pretence, which is a synonym for a fake show.

explanation.surface: Swimming shorts that show off the wearer's upper body.
explanation.definitionFit: Trunks are men's swimming shorts, and a trunk is also the main part of the human body.

parts.note: a son is a boy
attending somewhere is being at it, as in at school

explanation.surface: A boy giving his attention to a piece of music.
explanation.definitionFit: A sonata is a musical composition, typically for one or two instruments.

clue.text: King Henry's lead in unusual role of Robin Hood perhaps

indicators.note: in signals that these letters are placed inside the others
unusual signals that the letters of the words are made strange, rearranged

parts.note: K is the abbreviation for king in chess

indicators.note: a lead is what goes first, so only the opening letter is taken

explanation.surface: King Henry plays the lead in an unusual staging of the Robin Hood story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges ROLE OF to FOLERO, and 'in' places K and H inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Robin Hood is an example of a legendary popular champion celebrated in ballads.

parts.note: a pelt is an animal's skin with its fur
ore is mineral-bearing rock that is mined

explanation.surface: Hurling a mineral at someone causes a commotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pelt' reads as a verb, to throw things at, but it is the noun: an animal's hide.
explanation.definitionFit: A furore is an outburst of public anger or excitement, a synonym for uproar.

clue.text: Live accommodated by one encouraging soft drink

indicators.note: something accommodated by another is housed inside it

parts.note: a rooter is a supporter who cheers a team on, mainly in American usage
to be is to live or exist

explanation.surface: Living with a supportive person who keeps encouraging you to drink soft drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Root beer is a fizzy non-alcoholic drink flavoured with roots and herbs, mostly American.

parts.note: to bar is to ban, and the 's is read as 'is'

explanation.surface: A pub ban affecting a European involves harmful substances.
explanation.definitionFit: Bane originally meant a poison, as in wolfsbane, so harmful stuff fits.

clue.text: Occasion for people to enter test

indicators.note: to enter something is to go inside it

parts.note: the MOT is the annual roadworthiness test for British cars
men can mean people in general

explanation.surface: A time when people sit an exam.
explanation.walkthrough: The MOT, named for the old Ministry of Transport, is Britain's yearly safety test for older vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: A moment is a particular time or occasion, as in 'at that moment'.

parts.note: Harriet Harman is a Labour politician; dropping the h as the clue does with 'Arriet leaves her surname without its H
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A Cockney-sounding politician called Harriet needs one designer label.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped H of 'Arriet tells you to drop the H of her surname too: Harriet Harman was a senior Labour MP.
explanation.definitionFit: Giorgio Armani is a famous Italian couturier, an example of a fashion designer.

parts.note: cock is a familiar British term of address for a man, as in 'wotcha cock'; the 's is read as 'is'

explanation.surface: A matey bloke is a snob.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuck up' looks like snobbish, but here it means sticking upward, as a hat worn cocked.
explanation.definitionFit: Acock means tilted or turned upward, so literally standing up at an angle.

parts.note: an inn is a pub
an ovation is a burst of applause

explanation.surface: A novel pub wins applause from the drinkers.
explanation.definitionFit: An innovation is something newly introduced, a synonym for novelty.

parts.note: the ash is a common tree

explanation.surface: A cat abandoned up a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cat' is not the animal but the cat-o'-nine-tails, a whip.
explanation.definitionFit: The cat, short for cat-o'-nine-tails, is a whip, and a lash is a stroke or whip.

indicators.note: possessed by means held inside the other letters
possibly signals that the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A name that a woman might well have.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges LADY to LYDA, and N goes inside it; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lynda is a woman's given name, which a lady might indeed possess.

clue.text: Make dramatic entrance year after special occasion

indicators.note: after places this letter at the end
making something dramatic changes it theatrically, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Making a showy arrival a year after a big celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make dramatic entrance' reads as a stage direction, but only 'Make dramatic' signals the rearrangement of ENTRANCE into CENTENAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A centenary is a hundredth anniversary, celebrated as a special occasion.

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone wolfed down a dubious foreign vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: Eddo is the edible tropical root of taro, a starchy tuber from abroad.

indicators.note: turning means the word is read the other way round

parts.note: a man is a fellow
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A man who turns to drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: A handle is slang for a person's name, as in a CB radio handle.

clue.text: Space flight is rather aimless, creating news

parts.note: to moon about is to wander around aimlessly
a hot story is fresh and making news

explanation.surface: A rocket mission is drifting aimlessly yet still grabbing headlines.
explanation.definitionFit: A moonshot is a launch of a spacecraft towards the Moon.

explanation.surface: A puzzle that has to be marked as done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ticking off' looks like marking clues solved, but it means a telling-off: a cross word.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossword is a word puzzle, and a cross word is an angry rebuke, a ticking off.

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded on all sides by the other letters

parts.note: stats, short for statistics, are figures

explanation.surface: A university's ranking under pressure from the latest statistics.
explanation.definitionFit: Status is one's rank or standing in a social or professional order.

clue.text: Rock band keeping a stock of paper

indicators.note: keeping means holding the other letters inside

parts.note: R.E.M. was an American rock band

explanation.surface: A rock group stockpiling paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A ream is a quantity of paper, traditionally five hundred sheets.

clue.text: City in either end of yearbook

indicators.note: in places these letters inside the outer pair
either end of the word means its first and last letters

parts.note: either pairs with or, as in either this or that, so stands for OR

explanation.surface: A city appears at both ends of the annual.
explanation.definitionFit: York is a historic cathedral city in the north of England.

indicators.note: dashing means rushing about, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Gallant courage could turn shabby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seedy' looks like shabby, but it means to do with seeds.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovular relates to the ovule, the part of a plant that develops into a seed.

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: The grounds for a Spanish lady's distress.
explanation.definitionFit: A reason is a cause or motive, the grounds for something.

clue.text: Soft cryptic clue in Daily Telegraph initially

indicators.note: in places these letters inside the initials
initially means take the first letter of each word
cryptic means obscure or puzzling, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A gentle cryptic clue appearing in the Daily Telegraph.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter's own newspaper supplies D and T; 'cryptic' turns CLUE into ULCE between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Dulcet describes sweet, soft, pleasing sounds, as in dulcet tones.

indicators.note: around means one piece goes round the other

parts.note: the cod is a fish

explanation.surface: Fish circling a lake on a dreary day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bleak' is also a small freshwater fish, a tempting definition beside 'Fish', but here it means chilly.
explanation.definitionFit: Bleak weather is cold and raw, so cold is a synonym.

indicators.note: dressed means arranged or prepared, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A bird dressed in a way that suits me.
explanation.definitionFit: Titmouse is the full name of the tit, a small songbird.

clue.text: Second person in the Bible gets short measure

explanation.surface: A biblical figure is short-changed.
explanation.definitionFit: Thou is the archaic second-person pronoun used in the Bible, and a thou is a thousandth of an inch.

clue.text: One's sworn in supremo at Hogwarts

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A pledge taken by the headmaster at the Harry Potter school.
explanation.walkthrough: Hogwarts is the wizarding school in the Harry Potter books.
explanation.definitionFit: An oath is a solemn promise that a person swears.

indicators.note: constituting means forming or making up, so the letters build something new

explanation.surface: Peerages that make me a lord.
explanation.definitionFit: Earldoms are the ranks or titles held by earls.

clue.text: Get the better of remote American media company

parts.note: out can mean remote, as in an outlying place
Fox is the American broadcasting and film company

explanation.surface: Beating a distant American broadcaster.
explanation.definitionFit: To outfox is to outwit someone, getting the better of them by cunning.
